sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Avoid — governance under the framework override, not a finding of fraud. Signed annual CARO is more consequential than the RHP arm’s-length assertion: it criticizes related-loan terms and interest compliance. Brokerage growth is substantial, but IPO capital is moving into developer and connected-entity risk. Conditional financing models are provided, not an investable target. [S2] [S4]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Primary business is real-estate brokerage/leasing and mandates, with prior loan syndication. It is not a direct hotel operator: Veda develops/sells units, while unit purchasers receive lease-back revenue and related facility manager/BestWestern licensee receive their contractual fees. Issuer owns76%of developer, which owns44.92%of landowner; these interests do not entitle issuer to100%hotel receipts. Hummingbird41%associate is separate. [S2] [S6]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Developer relationships and exclusive inventory access offer ordinary differentiation. Some arrangements are verbal and customers have no long-term commitment; new identified mandates are documented and require refundable deposits. Largest customer concentration fell55.68%→17.56%, but top10still87.61%. Historical fee margins are not proof of an enduring moat or comparable to developer margins. [S2]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Developer counterparty failure can impair mandates and brokerage commissions together. Project delay increases17%financing cost and can require refinancing before sales. Bear model exceeds30crfacility by11.76cr and carries debt into contractual amortization periods; its calculated value assumes unsupported rescue funding and can overstate realizable recovery. Related-asset writeoffs and weak contracts can destroy capital despite profitable fees. [S2] [S4]

GOV.reason: Specific signed auditor criticism of related-loan terms and interest compliance, plus governance/reporting discrepancies, warrants low governance. Positive IFC/edit-log and disclosed repayments are counterevidence. Pending litigation is not used as proof of guilt.

MOAT.reason: Developer relationships and mandate access provide ordinary differentiation, but verbal/nonexclusive elements, heavy concentration and property-cycle dependence limit durable pricing power.

REV.reason: Strong multi-year brokerage sales growth and improved largest-customer diversification, offset by top10concentration, weakerPATgrowth and cyclicality. Project GDV is not recurring issuer revenue.

DUR.reason: Brokerage/mandate demand and approved projects provide a tangible but ordinary runway; development execution and high-cost financing constrain duration.

CAP.reason: High average asset-light returns coexist with about5%incremental all-capital return and large related/project exposures. New projects are immature; low score reflects allocation economics and loan terms, not automatic assumption of zero recovery.

CASH.reason: Three-year cash conversion.741x is middling, with FY25negative andFY26improvement financed materially by advances. No persistentCASH≤3cap is inferred.

BAL.reason: IPO improves parent liquidity but is earmarked; group project debt at17% and substantial connected capital exposures increase stress. Promoter guarantees are not issuer cash or automatic parent debt.

EXEC.reason: Brokerage growth delivered, but new development is unproven and related-loan controls are deficient. RERA registration is progress, not completion or profitability.

EARN.reason: Core fees drive earnings, but group acquisition/WIP and parent-report discrepancies require caution. Positive audit opinion does not remove specific CARO findings.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Governance override excludes ranking; conservative factor arithmetic retained. Conditional models do not cure deficient related-loan terms.
